body: FLAGS: net losses through 2002, near-zero GAAP margins for most of 1997-2015, P/E meaningless or in the hundreds, rising capex (fulfilment centres, then AWS data centres); FCF negative again in 2021-22 during a warehouse over-build [2021-22 FCF magnitudes from memory, unverified]. CONTEXT: (1) negative working capital: customers paid Amazon before Amazon paid suppliers, so growth released cash; (2) management explicitly targeted FCF per share, not EPS (1997 letter); (3) expenses that looked like opex (Prime shipping, AWS R&D) were investments with high incremental returns; (4) AWS, broken out only in 2015, was a hidden high-margin segment. IPO $18 in 1997 = ~$0.075 split-adjusted -> ~$188 (Jul 2021), ~2,500x, through a -94% drawdown (1999-2001). WHERE THE FLAG WAS RIGHT: in 1999-2001 the valuation was absurd and the stock lost 94%; the business flag (no profits) was false, the price flag was true. LESSON: when reported profit is suppressed by deliberate reinvestment, look at gross profit growth, CFO, working-capital sign and segment economics; but a false business flag does not protect you from a valuation crash.

data.context: negative WC, FCF/share focus, reinvestment, hidden AWS segment
data.flag: no profits; high capex; meaningless P/E
data.lesson: look through suppressed EPS but respect valuation
data.verdict: business flag false; price flag true in 1999

title: False alarm: Amazon's missing profits and heavy capex
